lesson_title: From Lisbon to Calicut to Table Bay
hook_text: Ten months at sea to reach India, and half the crew never came home. Why did a vegetable garden in Cape Town follow?
clip_script: July 1497. Vasco da Gama leaves Lisbon with four ships. He sails far out into the Atlantic, rounds the Cape, trades with Khoikhoi herders at Mossel Bay and names the coast of Natal on Christmas Day. In East Africa, a pilot guides him across the Indian Ocean. May 1498: Calicut in India. The sea route to the East is open. A century and a half later, the Dutch East India Company plants a garden at Table Bay to feed its sailors. Jan van Riebeeck arrives in 1652, and life at the Cape changes for ever.
visual_style: Whiteboard map tracing da Gama's route from Lisbon around Africa to Calicut, then a zoom to Table Bay with a small fort, a vegetable garden and Khoikhoi cattle on the slopes.
pacing: Steady voyage with dated stops, a pause at Calicut, then a slower close on the Cape and its people.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and trace da Gama's route on a map of Africa, marking every stop.
